bugs: Searching for "0" is ignored: Product::search uses `$query->when($term, ...)` and "0" is falsy, so /products?q=0 returns every product (confirmed with a probe). app/Models/Product.php:73. The same falsy-`when` pattern is in inCategory at app/Models/Product.php:85.

If someone opens /products?sort=bogus directly, the redirect sends them to the welcome page, which never renders $errors. They see neither the error nor the catalogue (routes/web.php:7, IndexProductRequest).
antipatterns: Logic in the view: `collect($sorts)->mapWithKeys(fn ($sort) => [$sort->value => $sort->label()])` builds the sort options inside the Blade template (resources/views/products/index.blade.php:20). This belongs in the controller or the enum.
Product::related() runs a query from a model instance method and uses a RELATED_LIMIT constant (app/Models/Product.php:23,52). That is more ceremony than a relatedTo scope.
A custom pagination view (resources/views/pagination/catalogue.blade.php) plus Paginator::defaultView. This works but adds code where a built-in simple view would do.

Every string is wrapped in __(), including trans_choice('{1} :count in stock|[2,*] :count in stock'), where both branches produce the same text (resources/views/products/show.blade.php:10). This is pointless ceremony.
cascadeOnDelete on category_id silently deletes products when a category is deleted (database/migrations/2026_01_01_000001_create_products_table.php:13).
The test helper builds route params with a convoluted inline ternary (tests/Feature/Admin/ProductManagementTest.php:27).
strengths: Uses modern Blade throughout: @session in the flash component, @props/$attributes->class()->merge() on form components, @selected/@checked, @error extracted into an <x-form.error> component.
One shared product-form component with a configurable submit label. Uses old() with the model value as fallback, and a hidden checkbox input so an unchecked box saves as inactive.
Thin controllers. Form requests use prepareForValidation to generate the slug, Rule::enum and Rule::unique()->ignore. Typed accessors on IndexProductRequest.
Modern Eloquent: #[Scope] attributes, #[Fillable], Attribute::get accessor, whereBelongsTo, whereRelation, LIKE wildcard escaping, deterministic tie-break ordering, eager loading of category.
Inline CSS, so pages render without compiled assets, and there is a test asserting that. The filter form reuses the shared select component.

bugs: An invalid filter query (for example ?sort=bogus) triggers a redirect-back from the GET form request instead of falling back to defaults. It recovers via / → /products, which shows the errors, but this UX is harsher than it needs to be (app/Http/Requests/IndexProductRequest.php).
antipatterns: The ProductSort enum has an apply(Builder) method, which puts query building inside an enum (app/Enums/ProductSort.php:22). A match inside the sortedBy scope would keep query logic on the model.

ProductPolicy has four identical is_admin methods, and the route middleware only checks viewAny, so create/update/delete are never consulted (app/Policies/ProductPolicy.php, routes/web.php:13). A single Gate would be simpler.
formattedPrice() is a plain method rather than an Attribute accessor (app/Models/Product.php:40). Minor.
The sort filter is hand-rolled markup instead of reusing the x-form.select component, and @selected compares against $filters['category'] ?? null (resources/views/products/index.blade.php:10-24).
The new checkbox component also renders @error itself, duplicating x-form.field (resources/views/components/form/checkbox.blade.php:9).
strengths: Search uses filled(), so "0" is a valid search term (probe passed), and LIKE wildcards are escaped.

Well-composed components: x-form.field wraps label, slot and @error, and input/select/textarea compose on top of it. Uses $attributes->class, @selected/@checked, old() with model fallback, and a hidden input for the checkbox.
Thin controllers using to_route()->with('status'), relatedTo/inCategory/search/active #[Scope] scopes, whereBelongsTo and whereKeyNot. The filters array comes from $request->safe()->only().
restrictOnDelete on category FK, composite indexes for the catalogue queries, Model::shouldBeStrict, and eager loading where it is needed.

Strong Pest tests. Datasets cover access for guests and non-admins on every route and each validation rule. followingRedirects proves errors and old input appear in the rendered form (including the selected category). Covers pagination links with preserved filters, page 2 count, empty filters, invalid query input, and an unchecked checkbox.

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-2 first. Both suites pass (impl-2: 44 tests, impl-1: 45), and the two apps are structurally almost identical: same FormRequests, #[Scope] scopes, enum sort, shared product-form component, inline-CSS layout and to_route flash redirects.

The deciding factor was one probe. In impl-1, /products?q=0 returns every product, because the search scope uses `when($term)` and "0" is falsy. impl-2 uses filled(), so that search works. impl-1 also sends someone who opens an invalid filter URL directly to a welcome page that never shows errors, while impl-2 lands them on /products with the errors listed.

On idioms, impl-1 does better in places: @session, an Attribute accessor, a dedicated <x-form.error> component and reuse of the select component in the filter form. It loses ground elsewhere: it builds a collection in the view, wraps everything in __() (including a no-op trans_choice), adds a custom pagination view, and cascade-deletes products when a category is deleted.

impl-2 also has rough edges: query logic inside the enum, and a four-method policy where only viewAny is ever enforced. Its tests are slightly stronger, since they render the redirected form to check that errors and old input actually appear.
